cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: el apoyo psicológico – (noun) la ayuda profesional orientada al bienestar emocional.

p.em: Example: El tratamiento brinda un valioso apoyo psicológico durante la crisis.

cosy-blockquote.p: la empatía (f.) ≠ la apatía (f.) – (noun) la capacidad de comprender el dolor ajeno frente a la indiferencia.

p.em: Example: La empatía del terapeuta permite construir un diálogo sincero.

cosy-blockquote.p: la confianza terapéutica – (noun) la seguridad mutua establecida entre profesional y paciente.

p.em: Example: La confianza terapéutica es esencial para sanar viejas heridas.

cosy-blockquote.p: la vulnerabilidad (f.) ≠ la invulnerabilidad (f.) – (noun) la apertura emocional sin miedo a la fragilidad.

p.em: Example: Aceptar la vulnerabilidad propia es el primer paso hacia la recuperación.

cosy-blockquote.p: la vulnerabilidad mental – (noun) el estado de fragilidad o sensibilidad emocional.

p.em: Example: El protagonista aprende a gestionar su vulnerabilidad mental sin culpa.

cosy-blockquote.p: abrirse – (verb) expresar los sentimientos y pensamientos más íntimos con confianza.

p.em: Example: Al paciente le cuesta abrirse durante las primeras sesiones de terapia.

cosy-blockquote.p: la vulnerabilidad – (noun) la cualidad de mostrar las emociones con sinceridad.

p.em: Example: Mostrar vulnerabilidad ayuda a conectar de forma auténtica con los demás.

cosy-blockquote.p: la empatía – (noun) la facultad de ponerse en el lugar de otra persona.

p.em: Example: La empatía compartida fortalece el vínculo afectivo entre los personajes.

cosy-blockquote.p: la confianza – (noun) la fe o seguridad firme que se deposita en alguien.

p.em: Example: Recuperar la confianza exige tiempo, paciencia y pequeños pasos cotidianos.

cosy-blockquote.p: el psicoterapeuta / la psicoterapeuta – (noun) el profesional de la salud mental que guía el proceso de sanación.

p.em: Example: La psicoterapeuta acompaña el proceso de autodescubrimiento con gran respeto.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does the opening of 'Lending My Wings' show the idea of psychological support? Practice with contextual Conversational Structures.
★ If you were in 'Lending My Wings', how would you handle the challenges of psychological support?

How does the director introduce empathy early in the movie? Focus on contextual Conversational Structures.
★ Have you ever faced a problem where you had to deal with empathy?

As the story goes on, does therapeutic trust create problems for the therapist? Frame your answer with contextual Conversational Structures.
★ Does the way the movie shows therapeutic trust feel like real life to you?

How do the scenes in 'Lending My Wings' show vulnerability between the main characters? Use contextual Conversational Structures.
★ How do you personally keep vulnerability in balance in your life?

How does the therapist react to the challenge of vulnerabilidad mental? Discuss using contextual Conversational Structures.
★ If you could change one decision made by the therapist about vulnerabilidad mental, what would it be?

What clues and secrets about 'abrirse' can you find in the movie? Use contextual Conversational Structures.
★ Have you ever used a word or expression like 'abrirse' in your own life?

How does the script use the expression 'vulnerabilidad' to make the scene more interesting? Respond with contextual Conversational Structures.
★ Do you think learning casual words like 'vulnerabilidad' is helpful for fluency?

How does using 'empatía' show the characters' real feelings during building therapeutic trust and exploring emotional vulnerability? Formulate with contextual Conversational Structures.
★ Is there an equivalent word in your language for 'empatía'?

How does learning the truth about 'confianza' change what you think of the characters? Analyze with contextual Conversational Structures.
★ When you want to express a feeling, do you use slang or direct words like 'confianza'?

If they knew the truth about 'psicoterapeuta' earlier, how would the story change? Speculate using contextual Conversational Structures.
★ What is your favorite line of dialogue from the movie 'Lending My Wings'?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
'the therapist's story of psychological support in 'Lending My Wings' is very sad, and they should be more careful.' Do you agree? Use contextual Conversational Structures.
★ If you were a director, how would you show the concept of psychological support?

'the therapist's movie makes the world look too beautiful, but it has a high cost.' Discuss using contextual Conversational Structures.
★ Do you think the visuals of a movie are more powerful than the dialogue?

'the therapist is not a nice person because they only care about therapeutic trust.' Give your opinion using contextual Conversational Structures.
★ Have you ever felt that a movie's alternative ending would be better?

'the therapist's movie 'Lending My Wings' is too simple and does not show deep feelings about vulnerability.' Talk about this with contextual Conversational Structures.
★ If you could choose a song from your life to match the theme of vulnerability, what would it be?

'the therapist's problem of building therapeutic trust and exploring emotional vulnerability never ends because they cannot agree on vulnerabilidad mental.' Explain using contextual Conversational Structures.
★ What was the most memorable scene in 'Lending My Wings' that made you think?

'The film would be better if the director chose a different setting for 'Lending My Wings'.' Speculate using contextual Conversational Structures.
★ Would you ever want to write a story based on your own life experiences?

'The secondary characters, like her patients, colleagues, and family members, are more interesting than the main hero.' Evaluate with contextual Conversational Structures.
★ Which part of filmmaking (music, camera angles, lighting) has the biggest effect on you?

'The music and sound design are what make 'Lending My Wings' a great movie.' Discuss using contextual Conversational Structures.
★ If you could change the cast of 'Lending My Wings', which actors would you choose?

'The recurring visual symbols are important to understand the film's deeper meaning.' Discuss using contextual Conversational Structures.
★ Do you enjoy analyzing movies or do you prefer to just watch the story?

'The story of 'Lending My Wings' is a critique of real-world human behavior.' Discuss using contextual Conversational Structures.
★ If you could save only one scene from 'Lending My Wings', which one would it be?

ul.li: Incorrect: I will resign if they skimp always on budget → Correct: I will resign if they always skimp on budget (Frequency adverbs like 'always' come before the main verb.)
Incorrect: We are living here since two years → Correct: We have been living here for two years (Use present perfect continuous with 'for' to express duration.)
Incorrect: They don't allow her leave the house → Correct: They don't allow her to leave the house (Use 'allow someone to do something' construction.)
